chapter_theme: Cutting off craving (அவா அறுத்தல்): talk of yogic technique is useless while desire remains; the Lord is found not in buildings or garb but in the heart freed of longing, and desire must be cut even where it reaches toward the Lord, for desire multiplies sorrow and its loss is bliss.
structure_note: The opening verses (2613 to 2616) give the command and its reasons; 2617 sets the ocean of desire against the Lord who holds the unfailing sea; the rest (2618 to 2622) describe the purity and attainments of those freed from desire and warn those who think themselves already saved.

2613.reading: There is no use sitting and babbling in all manner of ways about the breath and the needle; cut away desire and attachment, and once they are cut, the place where the Lord dwells becomes easy to reach.
2613.nuance: வாசி is traditionally the controlled breath of yoga; ஊசி (needle) is obscure, taken as the needle-fine central channel or the needle-point of concentration. அன்பு here, paired with ஆசை, is attachment to people and things rather than the love of the Lord Tirumular praises elsewhere.

2614.reading: He is not in the mansion, not in the hall, not in the courtyard, not in the temple, not in the holy garb; standing within the hidden place in the heart of those who have given up longing, he granted release.
2614.nuance: The list sweeps away both secular and sacred buildings and the ascetic's garb (வேடம்). மூடத்துள்ளே is unusual: மூடம் can mean dullness or a covered place, and is usually taken as the hidden inner space of the heart.

2615.reading: Cut off desire, cut off desire; cut off desire even if it is for the Lord; the more desire grows, the more sorrows come, and the more desire is let go, the more it becomes bliss.
2615.nuance: ஈசனோடாயினும் (even with the Lord) is the striking phrase. It is often taken as desire for gains or powers from the Lord, or even desire to be joined with him, which still keeps the self that wants; the verse itself doesn't narrow it.

2616.reading: Fling away the attachment that, together with the five oppressing elements, makes the path of suffering; letting go of longing is the knowledge that stands in truth, and what it reaches is the following of one's own self.
2616.nuance: அடுவன பூதங்கள் ஐந்தும் (the five elements that oppress) echoes Appar's அடுவன அஞ்சு பூதம், as Sengalvaraya notes. The last line, தொடுவது தம்மைத் தொடர்தலும் ஆமே, is compressed; it may mean that true knowledge turns one toward the self, or that what one clings to then follows one.

2617.reading: The ages, like the swelling sea at full moon, have passed; the gods slept, caught in one sea, and the people of the earth sank, caught in the sea of desire; the Lord stands holding the sea that never fails.
2617.nuance: The verse plays on four seas: உவா (the full-moon swell), துவா, அவா (desire) and தவா (unfailing). துவாக்கடல் is obscure; it may be the sea of duality or of the twofold deeds, or a corrupt word. Even the gods drown, only differently from humans.

2618.reading: The remaining deeds, disease and long labours ceasing and becoming pure, then even the five acts being turned back and grace gained directly, pressing close and sinking in: this is the purity of the knowers.
2618.nuance: நின்ற வினை may be the deeds still to be lived out (prarabdha). பின்றைங் கருமமும் is read as பின் ஐங்கருமமும், the five acts, perhaps the Lord's five acts or the soul's own five; பேர்த்து may mean they are reversed or set aside. துந்தொழில் is unclear.

2619.reading: Realising and attaining truth, the bright attainment is release; when infatuation with women is destroyed, the gain is the eight powers; if the firm knower gives up the Siva-body, after he reaches bountiful grace he comes to rest.
2619.nuance: The verse ranks attainments: the eight siddhis follow from mastering desire for women, but release follows only from truth. சிவகாயம் may be the body made Siva's through yoga, which the knower lays down; ஆறுமே may mean he is stilled or that his way is made.

2620.reading: Seeking in love, saying 'that one is the Lord', they do not grasp the truth that Siva here within is the Lord; this one of becoming is this birth of many kinds, and this one's world goes when its falseness is seen.
2620.nuance: The verse is built on a chain of pronouns and names: அவன், இவன், சிவன், பவன், புவன். The contrast between அவன் (that one, far off) and இவன் (this one, near) is the plainest point: people look for the Lord out there. பவன் and புவன் may be names of Siva or plays on becoming (bhava) and world (bhuvana).

2621.reading: The way things boil and the way they cool, the way they are set across this whole earth: the world does not seek the five who ordain it, and in this fermenting body there is a single thread.
2621.nuance: விதிக்கின்ற ஐவர் may be the five deities of the five acts or the five senses that command the body; நூல் ஒன்று may be one thread, one rule or one scripture. How the verse bears on desire is not clear from the Tamil.

2622.reading: You say 'we are saved' yet do not see the thing to be reached; if you set Nandi, who mingles in the fragrant flower, in your thought and join him with clarity, he is the root seed even before birth.
2622.nuance: கந்த மலர் (the fragrant flower) is traditionally the heart-lotus. முந்தைப் பிறவிக்கு மூலவித்து can mean the Lord is the primal seed prior to all birth, or that joining him reaches the root seed of births and so ends them.

links.note: Both make cutting desire the one test that counts: the Kural says only those free of desire are truly free, Tirumular says yogic talk of breath is useless until desire and attachment are cut.

In verse 298 Tirumular says if you cling, cling to the Supreme; here he says cut desire even if it is for the Lord. The conflict holds if ஆசை here is the same as பற்று there; if 2615 means desire for gains from the Lord, the two fit.

The Kural tells the renouncer to cling to the one free of clinging as the means of letting go; Tirumular tells him to cut desire even for the Lord. It depends on reading ஈசனோடாயினும் as desire directed at the Lord himself.
Both say desire is the source of sorrow and its ending brings unbroken joy: the Kural calls desire the sorrow of sorrows, Tirumular says bliss grows as desire is let go.
Both tie release to mastering the longing (வேட்கை) that works through the five: the Naladiyar has it guarded at the five gates of the senses, Tirumular has it flung away with the five elements.
Both set அவா (desire) beside தவா (unfailing): the Kural calls desire the seed of unfailing births, Tirumular has humans sunk in the sea of desire while the Lord holds the unfailing sea.
Both deny the Lord a dwelling outside the person: 2614 says he is in no mansion, hall or temple but in the desireless heart, 2650 says this one's house is his only house.

source_issues: 2617: துவாக்கடல் is obscure and may be corrupt.
2618: துந்தொழில் is unclear; it may be a misreading of துன்தொழில் (evil acts).
